passage.quote:
Collective execution describes instructions that coordinate a group of threads.
A block barrier makes arriving threads wait until their peers have arrived, then
lets them continue with the memory ordering promised by that barrier. Waiting,
completion, and reuse must follow the actual instructions and participant group.

summary: Coordinate actual arrivals, waiting and completion for a full-participation CTA barrier, keeping successive uses distinct.
Connect collective control to memory ordering and separately prove safety, completed results and finite execution existence.
remaining: Full-participation control, a structural completed-phase order projection and a conservative extension of memory constraints are proved. Actual fetched shared-memory/barrier instructions, derivation of the phase certificate from their execution, and a complete shared-memory kernel witness remain unimplemented.
